about: The epistola of the formulary “Saint Stephen, the First Martyr” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: In those days, full of grace and strength, Stephen was working wonders and great signs among the people. Then there arose certain men of the so-called synagogue of the Freedmen, and the Cyrenians, and the Alexandrians, and those who were from Cilicia and Asia, arguing with Stephen; and they could not resist the wisdom and the Spirit who was speaking. Now hearing this, they were cut through in their hearts, and they were grinding their teeth against him. But Stephen, filled with the Holy Spirit, gazing intently into heaven, saw God’s glory, and Jesus standing at God’s right hand. And he said: Behold, I see the heavens open, and the Son of Man standing at God’s right hand. But shouting in a loud voice, they stopped their ears, and with one accord rushed upon him. And casting him outside the city, they were stoning him; and the witnesses put down their garments beside the feet of a youth who was called Saul. And they were stoning Stephen while he was praying and saying: Lord Jesus, accept my spirit. Then, kneeling down, he cried aloud, saying: Lord, do not charge them with this sin. And when he had said this, he fell asleep in the Lord.
